info.title: SoftTrack
info.description: An open-source, self-hostable issue tracker inspired by Linear.

get.description:
What the sign-in and sign-up pages need before anyone has a token.

Public by necessity: the register page has to know whether to show a form
or an "ask an admin for a link" notice, and it asks before authenticating.
It reveals only that this instance is invite-only, which its sign-up page
would say out loud anyway.

post.description: Change the password, and return a token so this tab stays signed in.

get.description:
Story-point rollups by column and by assignee for the whole team.

Separate from the issue list because the list is paginated: summing a page
would silently report the total of whatever the client happened to load.

delete.description:
Delete an issue and everything that only existed because of it.

Attachments go with it, bytes included -- see
`lib_softtrack/issues.py`. Sub-issues do not: they are promoted to top
level rather than destroyed.

get.description:
Every relationship this issue has, grouped by how it reads from here.

A `blocks` row appears under `blocks` for the source issue and under
`blocked_by` for the target -- one stored row, two readings.

post.description:
Attach a file to an issue.

The file starts out belonging to the issue. Posting a comment with its id
in `attachment_ids` moves it to that comment -- which is the order the
interface needs, because a screenshot is pasted before the sentence about
it is written.

get.description:
Files attached to the issue itself.

Files belonging to a comment are returned with that comment instead, so
nothing appears twice.

schema.title: Response List Issue Attachments Issues  Issue Id  Attachments Get

get.description: The bytes. Authenticated like every other route, which means an `` cannot fetch it directly -- the browser sends no Authorization header. The frontend loads images through the API client and renders the result as a blob URL. The alternative, a token in the URL, would put a credential into every issue description that embeds an image and into every log line that records the request.

delete.description:
Remove an attachment and its bytes.

Any member of the team may, which matches how the rest of the app treats
issues and comments: membership is the boundary, and there is no
per-object ownership anywhere else to be consistent with.

schema.title: Response List Cycles Teams  Team Id  Cycles Get

post.description: Make this the team's active cycle. Only one may be active at a time.

Close the cycle, carrying unfinished issues into the next one.

Nothing is deleted: if there is no later cycle to carry into, the
unfinished issues go back to the backlog.

get.description:
Points and issues outstanding on each day of the cycle.

Carries the burnup line and the days scope moved, from the same data --
a burndown that hides scope changes makes a team look slow when what
actually happened is that the sprint grew.
Committed and completed points for recent completed cycles.
Issue counts per status per day. Widening bands mean work is piling up.
Issues opened against issues closed, with the running backlog.

post.description:
Import a Jira export into this team.

Defaults to a dry run. The dry run takes exactly the same path as the real
one and rolls back at the end, so the report you approve is the report you
then get -- rather than a preview built by separate code that can drift
from what the import actually does.

get.description:
Search issue titles, descriptions and comments.

Always scoped to the teams the caller belongs to. Postgres uses full-text
search with stemming and relevance ranking; SQLite falls back to a
substring match.

parameters.name: team_id

schema.description: Restrict to one team. Defaults to every team you are in.
schema.title: Team Id

parameters.description: Restrict to one team. Defaults to every team you are in.

get.description:
Just the badge. Separate from the list because it is polled and the
list is not -- a poll that dragged fifty rows over the wire to render one
number would be paid for on every open tab.

Every view this person can see on the team, plus which one is default.

Not paginated. A team that has more saved views than fit in one response
has a different problem, and the sidebar renders all of them at once.

put.description:
Where everyone on the team lands. Team admins only, shared views only.

Returns the whole list rather than the view, because setting a default
also unsets the previous one and the sidebar has to redraw both.

Where *you* land on this team, overriding the team's default.

Clearing it falls back to the team's rather than to all issues: no
override means no preference, not a preference for nothing.

CycleCompletion.title: CycleCompletion
CycleCompletion.description: The result of completing a cycle.

CycleProgress.title: CycleProgress
CycleProgress.description:
How much of the cycle's work is done.

Issues and points are reported separately because they disagree, and the
disagreement is the interesting part: eight of ten issues done with two
points of thirty burned means the hard work is all still ahead.

CycleState.title: CycleState
CycleState.description:
Where a cycle is in its life.

Derived from dates would be simpler, but a team that forgets to start a
cycle on Monday should not have Monday counted against its burndown, and a
cycle that runs a day long should not silently complete itself and carry
work away. So the state is set deliberately and the dates are the plan.

DefaultViewUpdate.title: DefaultViewUpdate
DefaultViewUpdate.description: Null clears the default rather than setting one.

ImportReport.title: ImportReport
ImportReport.description:
What an import did, or would do.

The same shape for a dry run and a real one, so what you approve is
literally what you then get.

InvitePreview.title: InvitePreview
InvitePreview.description:
What the invite link shows to someone who is not signed in yet.

Deliberately thin. Anyone holding the link can read it, so it says enough
to decide whether to accept -- which team, from whom, as what -- and
nothing about the team's contents or its other members.

InviteRead.title: InviteRead
InviteRead.description:
A pending invitation, as an admin of the team (or its recipient) sees it.

Carries the token because there is no mail server: the link is copied out
of this response and sent by whatever the team already uses. Only ever
returned to a team admin or to the person the invite is addressed to.

estimate.title: Estimate
estimate.description: Story points on the scale 1, 2, 3, 5, 8. Null means not sized yet, which is distinct from an estimate of zero.

IssueLinkType.title: IssueLinkType
IssueLinkType.description:
How one issue relates to another.

Only three are stored. "Blocked by" and "duplicated by" are not types --
they are the same rows read from the other end, which is what keeps the
two issues from ever disagreeing about their relationship.

`relates_to` is symmetric, so it is stored once and shown identically on
both issues.

estimate.title: Estimate
estimate.description: Story points on the scale 1, 2, 3, 5, 8. Null means not sized yet, which is distinct from an estimate of zero.

LinkedIssue.title: LinkedIssue
LinkedIssue.description: Just enough of the other issue to render a row and click through.

NotificationIssue.title: NotificationIssue
NotificationIssue.description:
Enough of the issue to render the row and navigate to it.

`team_key` and `number` rather than a URL: the inbox links into the app's
own routes (`/:teamKey/issue/:issueNumber`), and a server-built path would
be a second place that has to change when they do.

NotificationKind.title: NotificationKind
NotificationKind.description:
Why a notification was raised.

Deliberately about *what happened*, not about how the recipient came to
care -- "someone commented" reads the same whether you are watching the
issue because you filed it or because you were assigned it. Which of
those is true is not information the inbox has any use for.

NotificationUpdate.title: NotificationUpdate
NotificationUpdate.description: Marking one notification read, or putting it back.

ParentRef.title: ParentRef
ParentRef.description: Just enough of the parent to render a breadcrumb.

ParsedIssue.title: ParsedIssue
ParsedIssue.description: One issue as read out of an export, before anything is written.

SavedViewUpdate.title: SavedViewUpdate
SavedViewUpdate.description:
Every field optional: renaming, re-filtering and sharing are separate
gestures in the UI and each sends only what it changed.

SavedViews.title: SavedViews
SavedViews.description:
The whole sidebar in one response.

The defaults come back with the list rather than from their own endpoint
because the sidebar cannot render a row without knowing whether it is
starred, and a second request would mean a frame where none of them are.

StatusLoad.title: StatusLoad
StatusLoad.description: The work sitting in one board column.

TeamUpdate.title: TeamUpdate
TeamUpdate.description:
What an admin may change about a team.

No `key`: identifiers like ENG-42 are already in commit messages, chat
logs and browser history, and renaming the prefix would strand every one
of them. See README.

UnreadCount.title: UnreadCount
UnreadCount.description: The badge. Its own endpoint because it is polled, and the inbox is not.

UserMatch.title: UserMatch
UserMatch.description: A person named in the export, and who they were matched to.

UserMe.title: UserMe
UserMe.description:
The signed-in user's own record.

A superset of UserPublic rather than a separate model: what the account
can do instance-wide is the user's business, and nobody else's, so it is
only ever returned for `me`.

ViewFilters.title: ViewFilters
ViewFilters.description:
What a view narrows the issue list to.

Nested rather than flattened into the view models so that the same shape
is what the board sends, what a view stores, and what the frontend keeps
in the URL -- one type to keep in step instead of three.

Null everywhere means "all issues", which is what an empty view is.
